purpose: Compact active-conversation context for reasoning about independent-artist music publishing, based on Bobby Borg and Michael Eames, Introduction to Music Publishing for Musicians: Business and Creative Perspectives for the New Music Industry (Rowman & Littlefield, 2021 EPUB). This is educational context, not legal advice.

assistant_operating_rules: Separate composition rights from master/sound-recording rights in every analysis.
Separate ownership, administration, licensing, collection, accounting, and payment.
Identify the exact asset and exact right at issue before giving recommendations.
Identify who currently owns or controls the right, what is being granted, term, territory, approval rights, income split, deductions, and reversion or termination.
Distinguish writer share from publisher share and cash compensation from master participation or publishing participation.
Do not assume payment automatically transfers rights or that creative contribution automatically creates agreed ownership.
Preserve chain of title with written confirmations, split sheets, registrations, assignments, licenses, work-for-hire status, sample/interpolation records, and amendments as relevant.
Flag current verification needs for law, rates, society rules, platform practices, forms, fees, tax, international collection, and market norms.

Recommend qualified review when ownership transfer, exclusivity, work-for-hire, warranties, indemnities, advances/recoupment, long terms, worldwide rights, samples, minors, disputes, tax, or entity matters are involved.
For independent artists, preserve long-term optionality while evaluating real value exchanged; do not automatically reject every deal.

core_distinctions.composition_vs_master: Composition covers song authorship such as lyrics/melody/music; master covers a specific sound recording. Sync, release, samples, and monetization often implicate both sides but they are not the same asset.
core_distinctions.writer_share_vs_publisher_share: Writer share is tied to songwriter participation; publisher share is the publishing/control/admin side. Splits and collections must be registered consistently.
core_distinctions.publisher_vs_administrator: A publisher may acquire/control and exploit rights depending on the deal; an administrator is generally paid to register, license, collect, and account while ownership may remain elsewhere, subject to contract.
core_distinctions.license_vs_assignment: A license permits use under defined terms; an assignment transfers ownership/control interests. Both require careful term, territory, scope, approval, and reversion review.
core_distinctions.advance_vs_income: An advance is money paid up front and generally recouped from future royalties before additional payments; it is not free money.

quick_question_framework: What exact work or recording is involved?
Is the issue composition, master, or both?
Who contributed what, and what written agreement exists?
Which right is at stake: mechanical, public performance, sync, print, digital, administration, assignment, or other?
Is the question about ownership, collection, licensing, administration, accounting, or payment?
What registrations, identifiers, splits, publisher information, and chain-of-title evidence exist?
What term, territory, exclusivity, deductions, approval rights, reversion, warranties, and indemnities are proposed?
What needs current verification or professional review?
usage_note: Use the full JSON and specialist registries when more detail or source traceability is needed; use this compact file only to keep future planning conversations aligned.

core_principles.principle: Copyright in a song protects the composition and grants control over defined uses.
A composition copyright forms when original musical or lyrical expression is fixed in tangible form.
Registration and notice are separate from copyright formation but affect proof, remedies, and administration.
A work-made-for-hire arrangement can move authorship or ownership away from the creator when legal requirements are met.
Joint works require clear written agreement because default ownership and control rules may not match collaborators’ expectations.
Master recordings are separate copyrights and must not be collapsed into composition ownership.
Mechanical, performance, synchronization, print, and digital-transmission income arise from different uses and routes.
PROs license and collect public-performance royalties, not every form of publishing income.
Synchronization transactions commonly implicate both song rights and master rights.
Interactive and non-interactive digital uses can require different rights and collection routes.
